message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We investigate near-threshold
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <a:mi>J</a:mi>
                      <a:mo>/</a:mo>
                      <a:mi>ψ</a:mi>
                    </a:math>
                    photoproduction off the nucleon, focusing on hadronic rescattering effects induced by open-charm meson-baryon intermediate states. Beyond the conventional Pomeron-exchange mechanism, the
                    <c:math xmlns:c="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <c:msup>
                        <c:mover accent="true">
                          <c:mi>D</c:mi>
                          <c:mo stretchy="false">¯</c:mo>
                        </c:mover>
                        <c:mn>0</c:mn>
                      </c:msup>
                      <c:msubsup>
                        <c:mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</c:mi>
                        <c:mi>c</c:mi>
                        <c:mo>+</c:mo>
                      </c:msubsup>
                    </c:math>
                    and
                    <h:math xmlns:h="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <h:msup>
                        <h:mover accent="true">
                          <h:mi>D</h:mi>
                          <h:mo stretchy="false">¯</h:mo>
                        </h:mover>
                        <h:mrow>
                          <h:mo>*</h:mo>
                          <h:mn>0</h:mn>
                        </h:mrow>
                      </h:msup>
                      <h:msubsup>
                        <h:mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</h:mi>
                        <h:mi>c</h:mi>
                        <h:mo>+</h:mo>
                      </h:msubsup>
                    </h:math>
                    channels are incorporated within an effective Lagrangian framework. The relevant production amplitudes are constructed at tree level from
                    <m:math xmlns:m="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <m:mi>t</m:mi>
                    </m:math>
                    -,
                    <o:math xmlns:o="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <o:mi>s</o:mi>
                    </o:math>
                    -, and
                    <q:math xmlns:q="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <q:mi>u</q:mi>
                    </q:math>
                    -channel diagrams in a gauge-invariant manner. The resulting total and
                    <s:math xmlns:s="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <s:mi>t</s:mi>
                    </s:math>
                    -dependent differential cross sections are compared with recent near-threshold data from the GlueX,
                    <u:math xmlns:u="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <u:mrow>
                        <u:mi>J</u:mi>
                        <u:mo>/</u:mo>
                        <u:mi>ψ</u:mi>
                        <u:mtext>−</u:mtext>
                        <u:mn>007</u:mn>
                      </u:mrow>
                    </u:math>
                    , and CLAS experiments at Jefferson Laboratory. We find that the open-charm rescattering contributions improve the description of the data, especially for the differential cross sections at large momentum transfer, and can generate cusplike enhancements near the
                    <w:math xmlns:w="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <w:msup>
                        <w:mover accent="true">
                          <w:mi>D</w:mi>
                          <w:mo stretchy="false">¯</w:mo>
                        </w:mover>
                        <w:mn>0</w:mn>
                      </w:msup>
                      <w:msubsup>
                        <w:mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</w:mi>
                        <w:mi>c</w:mi>
                        <w:mo>+</w:mo>
                      </w:msubsup>
                    </w:math>
                    and
                    <bb:math xmlns:bb="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <bb:msup>
                        <bb:mover accent="true">
                          <bb:mi>D</bb:mi>
                          <bb:mo stretchy="false">¯</bb:mo>
                        </bb:mover>
                        <bb:mrow>
                          <bb:mo>*</bb:mo>
                          <bb:mn>0</bb:mn>
                        </bb:mrow>
                      </bb:msup>
                      <bb:msubsup>
                        <bb:mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</bb:mi>
                        <bb:mi>c</bb:mi>
                        <bb:mo>+</bb:mo>
                      </bb:msubsup>
                    </bb:math>
                    thresholds within the present hadronic model. We further present model estimates for the associated open-charm production processes
                    <gb:math xmlns:gb="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <gb:mi>γ</gb:mi>
                      <gb:mi>p</gb:mi>
                      <gb:mo stretchy="false">→</gb:mo>
                      <gb:msup>
                        <gb:mover accent="true">
                          <gb:mi>D</gb:mi>
                          <gb:mo stretchy="false">¯</gb:mo>
                        </gb:mover>
                        <gb:mrow>
                          <gb:mo stretchy="false">(</gb:mo>
                          <gb:mo>*</gb:mo>
                          <gb:mo stretchy="false">)</gb:mo>
                          <gb:mn>0</gb:mn>
                        </gb:mrow>
                      </gb:msup>
                      <gb:msubsup>
                        <gb:mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</gb:mi>
                        <gb:mi>c</gb:mi>
                        <gb:mo>+</gb:mo>
                      </gb:msubsup>
                    </gb:math>
                    , with total cross sections of the order of a few nanobarns.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Rescattering effects in near-threshold
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <mml:mi>J</mml:mi>
                      <mml:mo>/</mml:mo>
                      <mml:mi>ψ</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    photoproduction
